items.readable_text:
Content:
Consider the following system of linear equations and its respective augmented matrix:
[MATH: 2x + 6y = − 2; 3x − y = 2]

Content:
If we can convert the augmented matrix [MATH: M] to row echelon form, then we can solve the system using back substitution.

Content:
The procedure for reducing [MATH: M] to row echelon form using elementary row operations is called Gaussian elimination. To perform Gaussian elimination on a [MATH: 2 \times 2] matrix, we use the following procedure.

Content:
Step 1: Consider the entry [MATH: a_{11}=2] of the coefficient matrix. This entry is called a pivot element. We want to make this entry equal to [MATH: 1]. So, the first elementary row operation will be
[MATH: R_1 := \dfrac{1}{2}R_1]
and we have
[MATH: M|∼[2|6|− 2; 3|− 1|2]|R_{1}:=(1)/(2)R_{1}; ∼[1|3|− 1; 3|− 1|2].]

Content:
Step 2: Consider the entry [MATH: a_{21}=3] below the first pivot element. We want to make this entry equal to [MATH: 0]. So, the second elementary row operation will be
[MATH: R_2 :=R_2+(-3)R_1]
and we have
[MATH: M|∼[1|3|− 1; 3|− 1|2]|R_{2}:=R_{2} + (− 3)R_{1}; ∼[1|3|− 1; 0|− 10|5].]

Content:
Step 3: Finally, consider the entry [MATH: a_{22}=-10]. This entry is the second pivot element, and we would like to make it equal to [MATH: 1]. So, the third elementary row operation will be
[MATH: R_2 :=\dfrac{1}{-10}R_2]
and we get [MATH: M] in row echelon form:
[MATH: M|∼[1|3|− 1; 0|− 10|5]|R_{2}:=(1)/(− 10)R_{2}; ∼[1|3|− 1; 0|1|− (1)/(2)].]

Content:
The system is now
[MATH: x + 3y = − 1; y = − (1)/(2),]

Content:
and we can apply back substitution. The final equation [MATH: y=-\dfrac{1}{2}] tells us the value of [MATH: y.] Substituting this value into the first equation, we get
[MATH: x+3 \left( -\dfrac{1}{2} \right) = -1
\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad
x=\dfrac{1}{2}.]
Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x=\dfrac{1}{2}] and [MATH: y=-\dfrac{1}{2}.] Or, in vector form, [MATH: \left< \dfrac{1}{2}, -\dfrac{1}{2} \right>.]

sections.normalized_html:
Reducing [MATH: M] to row echelon form, we have

[MATH: M|∼[1|2|0; 3|− 2|− 8]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} + (− 3)R_{1}; ∼[1|2|0; 0|− 8|− 8]|R_{2}|:= − (1)/(8)R_{2}; ∼[1|2|0; 0|1|1].]

The system is now [MATH: x + 2y = 0; y = 1,]

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation [MATH: y=1] tells us the value of [MATH: y.] Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

[MATH: x+2(1)=0 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x=-2.]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x=-2] and [MATH: y=1.] Or, in vector form, [MATH: \left< -2,1 \right>.]

Consider the system of linear equations
[MATH: − x + 5y = 5; x − 6y = 5.]
Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix [MATH: M] of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.

sections.normalized_html:
The augmented matrix for this system is

[MATH: − 1|5|5; 1|− 6|5]

Reducing [MATH: M] to row echelon form, we have

[MATH: M|∼[− 1|5|5; 1|− 6|5]|R_{1}|:= − R_{1}; ∼[1|− 5|− 5; 1|− 6|5]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} + (− 1)R_{1}; ∼[1|− 5|− 5; 0|− 1|10]|R_{2}|:= − R_{2}; ∼[1|− 5|− 5; 0|1|− 10].]

The system is now

[MATH: x − 5y = − 5; y = − 10,]

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation [MATH: y=-10] tells us the value of [MATH: y.] Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

[MATH: x-5(-10)=-5 \quad\Rightarrow\quad x=-55.]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x=-55] and [MATH: y=-10.] Or, in vector form, [MATH: \langle -55,-10 \rangle.]

[MATH: M|∼[− 1|5|5; 1|− 6|5]|R_{1}|:= − R_{1}; ∼[1|− 5|− 5; 1|− 6|5]|R_{2}|:=R_{2} + (− 1)R_{1}; ∼[1|− 5|− 5; 0|− 1|10]|R_{2}|:= − R_{2}; ∼[1|− 5|− 5; 0|1|− 10].]

The system is now

[MATH: x − 5y = − 5; y = − 10,]

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation [MATH: y=-10] tells us the value of [MATH: y.] Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

[MATH: x-5(-10)=-5
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
x=-55.]

Therefore, the solution is [MATH: x=-55] and [MATH: y=-10.] Or, in vector form, [MATH: \langle -55,-10 \rangle.]
